mechanism_narrative: The sustained upward trend in RETAIL_REC over the past four weeks indicates a growing public comfort with out-of-home activities, which will continue to drive retail and recreation mobility higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days, despite the observed upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: A significant week-on-week rebound in WORKPLACES mobility, as observed from t-1w to t-0w, signals a return to office-based work that will directly increase retail and recreation activity in the immediate two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 14 days following a week-on-week WORKPLACES increase of more than 5 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent improvement in both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility suggests a broader return to pre-pandemic commuting and work patterns, which will collectively boost retail and recreation visits over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, even when both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES show a positive trend over the preceding four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates a shift away from home-bound activities, freeing up time and willingness for retail and recreation, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days decreases or remains flat, despite a continuous decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility over the preceding four weeks in a reopening regime.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility exceeding 4% above baseline suggests a general increase in essential out-of-home movement, which often precedes or accompanies a rise in discretionary retail and recreation activity in the very short term.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not show an increase in the next 7 days following GROCERY_PHARM mobility being above 4% from baseline.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous improvement in PARKS and RETAIL_REC mobility indicates a general increase in public willingness to engage in out-of-home leisure activities, suggesting continued growth in retail and recreation over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decreases over the next 14 days despite both PARKS and RETAIL_REC showing an improving trend over the last two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A combined trend of decreasing RESIDENTIAL and increasing WORKPLACES mobility signifies a strong shift away from remote work, driving more people into urban centers and subsequently increasing retail and recreation activity over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 6% while WORKPLACES rises above -15%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days when RESIDENTIAL falls below 6% and WORKPLACES rises above -15% in a shift from remote work regime.

mechanism_narrative: The sustained recovery in TRANSIT station visits, moving closer to baseline, reflects increased public confidence in using shared transportation, which facilitates greater access to and participation in retail and recreation activities over the next week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains above -50% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the next 7 days, even if TRANSIT mobility remains above -50% for two consecutive weeks.
